# HLT-C5 extraction notes (A2)

Text: pdftotext -layout of the supplied PDF, saved in _text/full.txt (clean.txt is the same text with line numbers and page footers removed, for searching). Page numbers are the printed report pages; arabic page n = PDF page n + 34.

## Scope
- Headline sources, as instructed: abstract (p.vii-viii), scientific summary in full (Results, Study 2, Conclusions, Summary of key findings, p.xxv-xxxi) and Chapter 7, Overall conclusions and future research directions (p.87-89).
- The Conclusions sections of Chapter 5 (p.73) and Chapter 6 (p.84-85) are outside this scope; they are used only as basis for relations or in these notes.
- Repeated claims: where the same assertion recurs in near-identical words across abstract, scientific summary and Chapter 7, one claim row lists all locations (e.g. C6, C7, C10, C11, C16, C42). Separate rows are kept where wording differs in substance (e.g. C58 and C66; C18 and C4).

## Rows proposed
- findings: 55 (N 22, Q 33). transformations: 13 (all crosses_strand yes). claims: 75. relations: 48 (covers 38, backs 10, clashes 0). decisions: header only.

## Look at first
1. Transformations F15-F18 and F19 (deductive themes). The qualitative exploration (Chapter 4, p.40-45; method p.20) groups teams as "high-implementing" and "lower-implementing" by their implementation rate, and examines meetings "attended by more professional groups". A2 recorded these as cross-strand transformations (made_from F3, or F6;F7). If A1 rejects them, F15-F19 have Q roots only and C3, C4, C18, C68 lose joint status.
2. Transformations F46-F55 (study 2). The 68 statements (F46, Q) were made from the 16 metathemes (F26) and quantitative results (F10 is the example given, p.76: "for example"; other N findings may have been used but are not named). The panel ratings (F47-F55) are new data on those statements; A2 recorded them as made_from F46. If A1 accepts this chain, every claim on study 2 ratings (C9, C10, C11, C12, C14, C37, C63) traces to both Q and N roots. If A1 treats the ratings as new data (not a transformation), these become N-only (C9 Q-only).
3. Joint-claim count depends on 1 and 2: with all transformations endorsed, 13 joint claims (C3, C4, C9, C10, C11, C12, C13, C14, C16, C18, C37, C63, C68); without the deductive-theme transformations, 9; without either set, 2 (C13, C16, which are joint by direct rests_on).
4. Fit is recorded on direct rests_on strands. C3, C4, C18, C68 and the study 2 claims are marked single-strand although they are joint by tracing.
5. C4 "clear goals and processes". The abstract places the TCI odds ratio after "clear goals and processes and a good team climate". TCI domains include "team vision" and "task orientation" (p.xxv), so "clear goals and processes" might refer to TCI scores rather than to the qualitative comparison. A2 split C4 (qualitative, F15;F17;F18, following SS p.xxvi) from C5 (TCI, F8). Alternative: C4 rests on F8 as well.
6. C15 (non-implementation "commonly due to patient or family choice"). Table 12 (F14) shows patient/carer/family choice at 15%, while "other" (28%) and "reason not given" (21%) were more frequent. The claim is not contradicted but overstates the table.
7. C19 numbers differ from Chapter 3: SS gives median attendees 5 to 17 and two to six disciplines; Chapter 3 (p.23, Table 7) gives mean meeting size 5 to 28 and one to seven groups. A2 kept rests_on F1; the reviewer may judge whether F1 supports C19 as stated.
8. C53 ("No single team [...] met all of the recommendations") rests on nothing: no comparison of the 12 teams against the 21 indications is reported (also stated in Chapter 6, p.85).
9. Rule 3 cases left empty, with candidate findings: C60 (medically dominated teams implemented more; Discussion p.69 states it, candidates F3, F21); C62 (gradient despite cancer guideline use; candidates F13, F16); C64 ("our findings suggest disease-specific approaches", candidates F50, F52, F53).
10. C16 rests on F10, F11 (N) and F24, F25 (Q): the qualitative Theme 5 (p.44-45) ends with the same statement, so A2 proposed fit confirm. C17 backs C16 (R) uses the SS sentence order.
11. C11 "desirable and feasible" (F48): the questionnaire asked for level of support (p.77); no separate feasibility rating is reported. Strand N assigned because the statement is a summary of ratings by specialty; the basis is thin.
12. C43 "mediated by": no mediation analysis is reported. Recorded as summary claim covering C4, C5; it adds an inference beyond them.
13. F46 strand Q: the 68 statements are textual; the count is the only number. A1 may prefer N or treat F46 as not a finding.

## Relations not proposed
- C13 to C12 ("In part, this was a result of"): an explanation of C12, none of backs/covers fits cleanly.
- C53 to C54: juxtaposed in SS p.xxx; Chapter 6 p.85 draws a different conclusion from C53 ("room for improvement in all specialties").
- No clashes. C42 (multidisciplinarity not associated with effectiveness) and C66 (multidisciplinarity highly valued) can both hold.

## Other
- Quotes are verbatim from the extracted text with line breaks joined; "[...]" marks omissions; "/" in a claim joins two wordings of the same assertion from different locations.
- F12 (age, sex) and F45 (meetings an effective use of time) are main results not used by any headline claim.
- Mental health patients are under-represented in interviews (two patients, p.72), a limitation stated by S1, not registered as a finding.
